title: Go-to-Prod Contingency & Annotated Roadmap
content:
Executive summary:

This is an annotated go-to-prod roadmap focused on contingency options, operational signal thresholds, and a compact KPI tracker intended for the last 10 days before launch through T+14. The doc mixes runbook-level checks with working notes for squad-level owners. Goal: minimize ambiguity in triage decisions during the launch window and give Product Ops and SRE a single reference for rapid action and measured rollback.

High-level timeline (T-10 -> T+14):
- T-10 to T-7: Stability smoke + surge capacity rehearsal (traffic replay, synthetic spike run)
- T-6 to T-3: Canary traffic (5% then 25%) with feature flags and throttling knobs staged
- T-2 to T-0: Full prep, communications dry run, monitoring dashboards locked
- Launch day: Gradual ramp plan (0 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100%) with hold gates at each step
- T+0 to T+14: Post-launch sampling, quality evaluation, economic reconciliation (per-token cost vs baseline)

Roadmap lanes (annotated):
- Product (owner: Priya Kapoor): feature gating, toggle matrix, user messaging templates.
  - Note: confirm message localization for EU and APAC variants (TODO).
- Serving/runtime (owner: Liam Chen): capacity plan by model family, cold-start times, fallback model mapping.
  - Contingency: pre-warm fallback GPUs with quantized model A if primary model B exceeds latency SLO.
- Ops/SRE (owner: Miguel Alvarez): autoscale policies, throttles, alert runbooks, on-call rotation for launch 48h.
  - Add short-circuit policy: if 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m, drop new sessions to safe-mode routing.
- Observability (owner: Ava Martinez): dashboards, alert thresholds, token-level cost heatmap, quality drift monitors.

Compact KPI tracker (for the launch dashboard):
- Primary KPIs (must be green to proceed at each gate):
  1) 95th perc latency (inference) <= 350ms (region: us-west-2)
  2) 5xx error rate < 0.3% sustained for 10m
  3) Throughput vs commit: able to sustain 2.5x expected peak for 15m in stress test
  4) Cost per 1K tokens within 20% of projected (after batching/caching adjustments)
  5) Quality retention: rouge/embedding-similarity drop < 2% vs baseline for sample set
- Secondary signals (monitor, do not gate):
  - KV-cache hit rate, average queue length, model memory pressure, cold-start frequency

Readiness checklist (pre-launch quick-run):
- Preconditions (T-2):
  - All canaries have run in staging and production 24h with no unresolved P1s.
  - Rollback playbook validated and smoke-tested (1-click route remove + autoscaler reset).
  - Owner roster and escalation matrix published to #launch-ops Slack.
  - Billing alerts enabled for sudden spend (>2x expected burn)
- Launch day must-haves (on call):
  - Product Ops lead: Priya (primary), Ava (backup)
  - SRE lead: Miguel (primary), Liam (backup)
  - Clear purple-team for customer comms: CSM on standby

Contingency playbook (decision heuristics):
- Scenario A: Latency drift beyond gate (95p > 500ms)
  - Step 1: Reduce concurrency per worker by 25% (automated toggle)
  - Step 2: Route a portion (20%) of requests to distilled quantized model (lower cost, lower precision)
  - Step 3: If still failing after 5m, initiate slow-rollback to previous model snapshot and send incident note.
- Scenario B: Quality regression (sample QA shows >3% drop)
  - Immediate stop of traffic to new variant; divert to stable model pool.
  - Trigger evaluation job to run batched compare on last 10k requests.
  - Postmortem and hold decision required before re-try.
- Scenario C: Cost runaway
  - Threshold: projected monthly delta > $10k in first 72h.
  - Actions: enable throttling at gateway for non-critical routes; enable caching TTL extension; pause background scoring jobs.

Triage checklist (quick play for Pager duty holder):
- First 5 minutes: identify lane (latency/error/quality/cost). Post summary in incident channel with current KPIs.
- 5-15 min: apply the light-touch mitigations per lane (reduce concurrency, partial routing to fallback, toggle caching).
- 15-60 min: escalate to on-call leads if mitigations not restoring green KPIs. Begin customer comms if > 30m impact.

Assumptions and stress test notes (working):
- We assume mixed request size distribution: 60% short (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512). Adjust batching heuristics if real traffic shifts by >10% toward long.
- Synthetic spike test on T-8 used replay traffic x3 for 10m. Observed 95p latency +120ms; actionable: bump prefetch and KV-cache size.
- TODO: run a focused embedding-burst test against dedicated pool to validate memory compaction.

Launch day run-of-show (concise):
- 08:00 - final readiness readout (30m)
- 09:00 - begin canary ramp to 5%
- 09:30 - check KPIs, if green, ramp to 25%
- 10:30 - check KPIs, if green, warm additional nodes and ramp to 50%
- 11:30 - if green for 30m, full ramp to 100%
- Ongoing: hourly brief notes in #launch-ops for first 12h, then every 4h through T+48

Post-launch evaluation plan (T+1 -> T+14):
- Data collection: sample 1000 requests/day for quality checks against standard prompt set. Track hallucination and model drift.
- Economic reconciliation: actual tokens vs forecast, batch efficiency delta, cache hit delta. Create a reconciliation ticket by T+7.
- Retro: 72h quick retro, 14-day detailed retro with cross-functional recommendations.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm legal/regulatory messaging for EU customers re: private deployments (Priya).
- Get final cost estimate for quantized fallback pool (Liam).
- Decide SLA wording for customers on day-of rollbacks (Ava).

Appendix: useful quick links
- Confluence runbook: PRODOPS-482
- Canary dashboards: https://grafana.internal/uid/launch-canary
- Immediate rollback script: github.com/redwood/ops-scripts/rollback.sh

End of doc. This is intentionally concise; use the linked artifacts for deep steps. Keep this doc as the single-sentence runbook and gate reference during launch window.
